nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What alternative approach is proposed to monitor research efforts?
nodes.answer: The proposed alternative approach monitors the intended ex-ante research efforts in funded research projects to provide a complementary view of research activity.
nodes.paragraph: Methods include both quantitative bibliometric databases and qualitative thematic analysis (Xiao & Watson, 2019) using review protocols such as PICO(S), SPIDER, SPAR-4- SLR, PRISMA, and TOPIC+M (Methley et al., 2014; Mohamed Shaffril et al., 2021; Moher et al., 2009; Page et al., 2021). We refer to Mishra et al. (2024) and Ciarli et al. (2022) for such an SLR on SDGs and to Ralph and Arora (2024) for SDG 8 in particular. These approaches analyse finalized research output and, therefore, can be expected to be biased towards positive findings (Scheel et al., 2021). Moreover, given the lengthy peer review process and publication delays, SLRs may fail to provide a timely overview of the current research agenda. We propose an alternative approach that monitors the intended ex-ante research efforts in funded research projects, providing a complementary view of research activity to a standard SLR. The analysis traces the heterogeneity in past research and tracks whether currently funded projects are aligned with policy objectives.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Protected areas management|Research and monitoring teams_qna_002
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: Who are the members of the research team involved in this study?
nodes.answer: The research team includes senior researchers and graduate students representing various fields such as environmental studies, biology, history/Indigenous studies, fine arts, and nursing.
nodes.paragraph: This research is part of a broader research project that aims to develop an enhanced understanding of how different groups in Canadian society speak about and process the emotions associated with climate change and other forms of ecological loss. The project focuses on the Boreal and Atlantic ecoregions, two ecozones experiencing considerable impacts from climate change (e.g., increased wildfire numbers and severity and increased storm severity). The authors/research team includes diverse positionalities and roles in research (i.e., senior researchers and graduate students) representing environmental studies, biology, history/Indigenous studies, fine arts, and nursing. This subset of the more extensive study used a phenomenological approach to understand how observers experiences and learning adjacent to ecological loss impacted their emotions, decisions, and actions relative to their roles connecting to the environment. Specifically, our objectives were to: 1) Examine how environmental observers learn about the changing environment (i.e., through communications and (or) direct observation); 2) Explore how such learning impacts the emotional reactions of environmental observers; 3) Develop a deeper understanding of how emotional aspects of learning might be changing the actions (e.g., decision-making and (or) direct forms of action) of environmental observers; and, 4) Gain insight into how actions triggered by emotions might have the potential to transform those emotions.

nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What permits were issued for the research conducted in the Galapagos?
nodes.answer: The research was authorized under permits PC-51-18 and PC-59-19 issued by the Galapagos National Park Directorate.
nodes.paragraph: The climate of the Galapagos is heavily influenced by oceanic currents and winds, with vegetation distribution primarily deter - mined by orogenic rainfall [ 45, 46]. The islands of Santa Cruz, San Cristobal, Isabela, and Floreana are inhabited by humans, with an estimated population of 33,42 peo - ple living in the archipelago as of 2020 [ 47]. We carried out this study on San Cristobal, the easternmost island of the archipelago [ 44, 48]. San Cristobal, the fifth-largest island with an area of 558 km2, is also the geologically oldest island in the Galapagos [ 44, 49]. Ethics statement Our study was authorised under research permits PC-51 - 18 and PC-59-19, issued by the Galapagos National Park Mena et al. BMC Zoology (2025) 10:7 Directorate (Direcci n del Parque Nacional Gal pagos, Ministerio del Ambiente). We followed the guidelines for using wild birds in research by Fair et al. [ 50]. Study design and data collection This study was conducted as part of a monitoring pro - gramme of the land bird populations on San Cristobal Island.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Protected areas management|Research and monitoring teams_qna_004
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: Who supervised the pilot study documenting the new monitoring strategy?
nodes.answer: The study was supervised by scientific staff with expertise in mammalogy and molecular biology.
nodes.paragraph: In this way, small mammals can also be detected (Harper et al. 2019; Leempoel et al. 2020a, b). This latter method can be applied on a larger scale but again is limited by the inability to know the exact site of occur - rence of a detected species. The above review reflects the methodological and legal challenges that are associated with small mammal monitoring at small and large spatial and temporal scales. These challenges motivated us to develop a new monitoring strategy that combines non-invasive field sampling using baited tubes to collect fecal pellets and molecular species determination using the mitochondrial COI gene as a barcod- ing marker. Here we document the results of this pilot study to test the performance of our new monitoring strategy under large-scale conditions. The survey was performed under the supervision of scientific staff with expertise in mammalogy and molecular biology (study design and lab work). How - ever, the large spatial coverage and the high number of sam- ples is basically achieved by incorporating volunteers for fieldwork, e.g., rangers of national parks, citizen scientist or scientific staff without an explicit expertise in the field of DNA-barcoding.
